Maya Chen: Quick q — I started using a coworking hub in Boulder 3 days/week on a recurring basis. Still keeping SF as my official home base. Do I need to declare this anywhere for the WFH stipend / benefits / or payroll/tax stuff?
Sam Patel: Thanks for flagging this, Maya. Short answer: yes, we need a formal declaration if you regularly work from a secondary location. It can impact the WFH stipend proration and state tax withholding.
Maya Chen: Got it. Is this the same as a relocation? I’m not moving my home, just commuting a few days.
Sam Patel: Not a relocation. This is a "satellite worksite" scenario. Different rules:
- If you work in CO more than ~30 days total in a calendar year, payroll may need to withhold CO state income tax and we might have to notify our payroll provider.
- WFH stipend: company policy covers a monthly allowance for your declared primary home workspace. For recurring satellite use we typically handle an accommodation stipend/one-off setup payment, not duplicate monthly stipends, unless your manager requests a formal change.
Ava (Manager): I approve Maya using the Boulder space 3 days/wk. Team workload unaffected.
Jordan (Payroll): @Sam @Maya — please submit the Remote Work Location Declaration form so Payroll/Tax can review. We need your coworking address, effective start date, and an estimate of days/week there. If you’ll be there 3 days/week consistently, that crosses the threshold we use to assess nexus implications.
Maya Chen: link to form?
Sam Patel: Here — https://redwood.internal/people-ops/forms/remote-location-declaration (internal). Fill it out and attach the membership agreement or a screenshot of your monthly recurring booking so we have evidence of regular use.
Jordan (Payroll): Also include the effective date before payroll cutoff (payroll cutoff is every 15th and last day of month at 11:59PM PT). If submitted before the cutoff, changes can be effective the following payroll period; otherwise it will apply after the next cutoff.
Maya Chen: Ok submitting now. Do I need to fill a new state tax form?
Jordan (Payroll): Potentially. If we determine CO withholding is required, we'll ask you to complete any state-specific forms (e.g., Colorado Employee Withholding). We'll reach out with the exact form and next steps. Expect ~3–10 business days for Assessment + Payroll ops to process.
Sam Patel: One more logistics note: benefits (health/dental) usually stay the same if your legal home remains SF. But unemployment/employer tax registration is on the company side and may require action if we see several employees regularly working out of CO. We'll keep you posted.
Maya Chen: Thanks — submitted the form and attached the coworking invoice.
PeopleOps Bot: Form received: Remote Work Location Declaration (1901754321-001).
Jordan (Payroll): Received the docs, thanks Maya. We'll triage and loop in Tax if needed. If anything changes (more days, permanent move), please update the form.
Sam Patel: Thanks all — Maya, we'll follow up in-thread once Payroll confirms whether CO withholding or pro-rated stipend changes are required. :thumbsup:
